vulnerable_code:
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException

router = APIRouter(prefix="/_debug/runtime/plugins")

@router.get("/{plugin_id}/source-ast")
async def get_plugin_cached_ast(
    plugin_id: str,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    reload_engine: HotReloadEngine = Depends(get_reload_engine)
):
    cached_module = reload_engine.get_cached_plugin(plugin_id=plugin_id)
    if not cached_module:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Plugin module not found in reload cache")

    return {
        "plugin_id": plugin_id,
        "module_name": cached_module.name,
        "ast_dump": cached_module.ast_representation,
        "exported_symbols": cached_module.symbols
    }
diagnosis: The hot-reload debug endpoint dumps the AST and exported symbols of cached plugin modules using the plugin_id path parameter. Although it checks authentication, it does not enforce tenant ownership of plugin_id. An attacker can specify plugin IDs belonging to other enterprise tenants to inspect their proprietary algorithms, business logic ASTs, and internal hook implementations.

corrected_code:
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException

router = APIRouter(prefix="/_debug/runtime/plugins")

@router.get("/{plugin_id}/source-ast")
async def get_plugin_cached_ast(
    plugin_id: str,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    reload_engine: HotReloadEngine = Depends(get_reload_engine)
):
    cached_module = reload_engine.get_cached_plugin(plugin_id=plugin_id)
    if not cached_module or cached_module.tenant_id != current_user.tenant_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Plugin module not found in reload cache")

    return {
        "plugin_id": plugin_id,
        "module_name": cached_module.name,
        "ast_dump": cached_module.ast_representation,
        "exported_symbols": cached_module.symbols
    }
